security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, placeholder API key examples, and checklist text. The remaining concern is documentation that shows direct shell parameter substitution without safety guidance, which can lead authors to create injection-prone Enact tools.

remediation.issue: Command examples use direct parameter substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to validate inputs, prefer argv-style execution, and avoid passing untrusted values through a shell.

remediation.issue: Shell examples do not describe quoting boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Show safer command patterns and explain how Enact escapes or validates substituted parameters.

remediation.issue: Static scanners misread Markdown fences as executable backticks.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that listed commands are examples and not actions the skill should run without user approval.

content.value_statement: Creating Enact tools requires clear structure, schemas, commands, and publishing steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a compact reference for Enact authoring.
actual_capabilities: Explains the basic Enact tool folder structure and required enact.md file.
Summarizes commands for running, installing, searching, signing, and publishing tools.
Shows a reusable enact.md template with input schema, output schema, environment, and metadata fields.
Compares Python, Node.js, Rust, Go, and shell command examples for container tools.
Describes secret declaration and keyring-based setup for tool environment variables.
Provides a short checklist for validating tool metadata before publishing.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not a complete Enact project generator.
It does not verify that commands are safe for a specific host or repository.
It does not replace the official Enact documentation or release notes.
It does not validate published tools or marketplace permissions.

use_cases.title: Create a first Enact tool
use_cases.description: Use the guide to understand the required files, metadata fields, schemas, and local test command.

use_cases.title: Prepare a tool for publishing
use_cases.description: Review the signing, publishing, metadata, and checklist steps before sharing a tool.

use_cases.title: Teach agents Enact conventions
use_cases.description: Give an AI assistant a concise reference for Enact structure, command fields, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Enact basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Enact tool structure using this guide. Focus on the purpose of enact.md, main source files, and structured input and output.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an enact.md outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me outline an enact.md file for a tool that accepts one text input and returns one text result. Include required fields and schema notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a tool design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Enact tool plan against the guide checklist. Identify missing metadata, schema gaps, command concerns, and publishing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Harden command and secret usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Enact command field and environment variable plan. Recommend safer parameter handling, secret storage, and validation before publishing.

output_examples.input: I need a quick overview of what an Enact tool contains.
output_examples.output: An Enact tool usually includes an enact.md file and source code. The guide explains metadata, schemas, commands, environment variables, and publishing steps.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a tool before publishing.
output: Confirm the name, description, input schema, and output schema are complete.
Use a pinned container image and document dependency installation.
Test the tool locally, then sign and publish it only after review.

output_examples.input: How should I handle an API key in an Enact tool?
output_examples.output: Declare the variable as a secret in the tool metadata. Set it through the Enact environment command and avoid storing it in local environment files.

best_practices: Use the guide as a checklist before running or publishing Enact tools.
Validate inputs and outputs with schemas before relying on tool behavior.
Treat command and secret examples as templates that need project-specific review.
anti_patterns: Do not copy command templates without checking quoting and input validation.
Do not publish a tool before testing its schema and runtime output.
Do not place real secrets in documentation, prompts, or local environment files.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants explain Enact tool structure, commands, schemas, secrets, and publishing workflow.

faq.question: Does it create a complete tool automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that can support tool creation, review, and publishing preparation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown guide. Any command execution should require user review and approval.

faq.question: How does it describe secrets?
faq.answer: It shows secret metadata and recommends setting secret values through Enact instead of storing them in environment files.

faq.question: What should users review carefully?
faq.answer: Users should review command substitution, input validation, dependency installation, and publishing permissions before using examples.
